tasks.gr11-organic-chemistry-t3: Topic: Organic Chemistry — Hydrocarbons and Functional Groups. Cover homologous series: alkanes (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, single bonds), alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ, one C=C double bond), alkynes (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, one C≡C triple bond); functional groups: alcohols (–OH), carboxylic acids (–COOH), esters (–COO–), aldehydes (–CHO), ketones (C=O in chain), amines (–NH₂), amides (–CONH₂); IUPAC naming rules (identify parent chain, number from end nearest substituent, use correct suffix); and physical property trends within a series. Ask Grade 11 learners to name compounds using IUPAC rules, draw structural and condensed formulae, identify functional groups from structure, and explain boiling point trends.
tasks.gr11-intermolecular-forces-t3: Topic: Intermolecular Forces and Physical Properties. Cover types of intermolecular forces in increasing strength: London/dispersion forces (temporary dipoles, all molecules, increase with molar mass), dipole-dipole forces (permanent dipoles in polar molecules), and hydrogen bonding (N–H, O–H, F–H bonds only — strongest IMF); molecular polarity determined by bond polarity and shape (VSEPR: linear, bent, trigonal planar, tetrahedral); relationship between IMF type/strength and boiling point, melting point, viscosity, surface tension, and solubility ('like dissolves like'). Ask Grade 11 learners to identify IMF types, predict and explain boiling point trends, determine molecular polarity, and compare physical properties.
tasks.gr11-redox-reactions-t3: Topic: Oxidation, Reduction and Redox Reactions. Cover definitions: oxidation (loss of electrons, OIL), reduction (gain of electrons, RIG), the mnemonic OIL RIG; assigning oxidation numbers using rules (free elements = 0, monatomic ions = charge, oxygen = −2 except peroxides, hydrogen = +1 except metal hydrides, sum equals overall charge); identifying oxidising agents (gains electrons, is itself reduced) and reducing agents (loses electrons, is itself oxidised); and balancing redox half-reactions in acidic solution. Ask Grade 11 learners to assign oxidation numbers, identify redox processes, determine oxidising and reducing agents, and write balanced half-reactions.
tasks.gr11-electrochemical-cells-t3: Topic: Electrochemical Cells and Electrolysis. Cover galvanic cells: spontaneous redox reactions, anode (oxidation, negative electrode), cathode (reduction, positive electrode), salt bridge (maintains electrical neutrality), standard electrode potentials (E° from the Standard EMF table), cell EMF calculation (E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode); cell notation (anode | anode solution ‖ cathode solution | cathode); electrolytic cells: non-spontaneous, powered by external source, electrolysis of water and other electrolytes; products of electrolysis. Ask Grade 11 learners to label cell diagrams, calculate EMF using E° values, write half-reactions, compare galvanic and electrolytic cells, and predict electrolysis products.
tasks.gr11-electromagnetism-t3: Topic: Electromagnetism. Cover the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire (evidence from a compass, Right Hand Rule, field lines round a straight wire, a loop and a solenoid), electromagnets, magnetic flux Φ = BA cos θ with θ the angle between B and the normal, Faraday's law (induced emf proportional to the rate of change of flux), Lenz's law (the induced current opposes the change: the near end of a solenoid takes the same pole when a pole is pushed in and the opposite pole when it is pulled out), and the environmental impact of overhead cables in qualitative terms. Ask Grade 11 learners to give directions with the Right Hand Rule and to calculate flux.
tasks.gr11-energy-chemical-change-t3: Topic: Energy and chemical change. Cover bond breaking (endothermic) and bond forming (exothermic), enthalpy and the heat of reaction ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants) in kJ·mol⁻¹ (negative for exothermic, positive for endothermic), activation energy as the rise from the reactants to the peak, free-hand energy graphs, and everyday examples (combustion, respiration, photosynthesis, hand warmers, cold packs). Ask Grade 11 learners to find ΔH and activation energy from stated values.
tasks.gr11-acid-base-reactions-t3: Topic: Acid-base reactions. Cover the Arrhenius and Brønsted-Lowry definitions of acids and bases, conjugate acid-base pairs, ampholytes (water), balanced equations for acid + metal hydroxide, acid + metal oxide and acid + metal carbonate (salt + water, plus CO2 for a carbonate), indicators and a simple qualitative titration with its end point. Balance every equation. Ask Grade 11 learners to identify acids, bases and conjugate pairs and to write products.
